title: A Thorn for the Oath
premise: In the city of Vell, magic is outlawed and the Charmwright Guild has dwindled to three members who survive by selling trinkets that barely work. When a dying courier presses Lena Kavanagh a scorched map leading to the Emberhold, she discovers the king of Vell was replaced decades ago by a hollow thing sustained by stolen dragon-fire — the same fire that keeps her guild's last true charms alive. Pursued by the king's Unbinding Wardens and shadowed by a disgraced guildmaster who knows more than he admits, Lena follows the map into the mountain vaults where the real king lies bound. In the vaults she learns the courier was her presumed-dead mother, and that the binding can only be undone by someone with guild-blood who willingly gives up their own spark of magic. Lena unbinds the king, extinguishes the impostor, and chooses a life without magic — finding that belonging was never in her blood, but in the guild she rebuilds.
about_author: Bram Zhou is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing guild records in coastal port cities before turning to fiction. They write fantasy about inherited obligations and the quiet violence of institutions, and live near the sea with an unreasonable number of houseplants.

chapters.title: The Charm That Didn't Work
chapters.summary: Lena's POV. In Vell's night market, Lena sells a luck-charm that fails its buyer — a small humiliation that shows how far the guild has fallen. A Warden raid scatters the stalls, and she barely escapes with her stock. Emotional beat: weary resignation, the ache of pretending her inheritance still means something.

chapters.title: A Stranger's Last Bargain
chapters.summary: Lena's POV. A burned, dying courier collapses in the guildhall's back room and presses a scorched map into Lena's hands, whispering a word she hasn't heard in ten years: 'Emberhold.' Wardens arrive moments later; the stranger dies buying them time. Emotional beat: fear curdling into reluctant obligation — she cannot unknow what she now carries.

chapters.title: What the Guild Remembers
chapters.summary: Lena's POV. Lena begs the guild's last master, old Corvane, to explain the map. He refuses, burns a page of the guild ledger, and forbids her to leave. She goes anyway, stealing the guild's one working charm. Emotional beat: the first fracture — loyalty to the guild versus loyalty to the truth.

chapters.title: The Road Out of Vell
chapters.summary: Lena's POV, with an interlude from Warden-Sergeant Ilse tracking her. On the mountain road, Lena is caught by Ilse but escapes when a passing tinker — the disgraced guildmaster Dain — misdirects the Wardens with a charm he swore he'd never use again. Emotional beat: wary alliance; two exiles recognizing each other.

chapters.title: The Hollow Court
chapters.summary: Dain's POV. In a border town, Dain reveals what he knows: the king of Vell died thirty years ago, and something wears his crown, fed on dragon-fire siphoned from the Emberhold. The Wardens close in; the town burns as they flee. Emotional beat: horror and guilt — Dain once helped build the siphon.

chapters.title: Emberhold's Threshold
chapters.summary: Lena's POV. The map leads them to a sealed mountain gate that opens only to guild-blood. Lena's stolen charm flares true for the first time in her life — the mountain knows her. Inside, Wardens ambush them; Dain is gravely wounded holding the passage. Emotional beat: awe and terror as the inheritance becomes literal.

chapters.title: The King Beneath the Mountain
chapters.summary: Lena's POV. In the vaults, Lena finds the real king — alive, bound, dreaming — and the dying dragon whose fire feeds both his prison and the impostor's crown. The dragon shows her the binding's terms: only guild-blood, freely surrendered, can unmake it. Emotional beat: the weight of choice; the fire is guttering, and so is time.

chapters.title: The Mother's Map
chapters.summary: Lena's POV. Studying the map's marginalia, Lena recognizes her mother's handwriting — the courier was sent by, or was, the woman who vanished ten years ago, and the map was always meant for her. Ilse arrives, but hearing the truth, wavers. Emotional beat: grief transmuted into resolve; the personal made epic.

chapters.title: The Unbinding
chapters.summary: Lena's POV. As the last dragon-fire gutters, Lena begins the unbinding, surrendering her spark while Ilse turns against the Wardens and Dain, dying, holds the siphon open. The false king's crown cracks in Vell; the true king wakes. Emotional beat: sacrifice and release — Lena gives up magic and feels, for once, whole.

chapters.title: A Guild of Three, Rebuilt
chapters.summary: Lena's POV, months later. The king, restored but changed, lifts the ban on guild-charms. Lena, magicless, reopens the guildhall with new apprentices who need teaching more than trinkets. The ember from the dragon's last breath sits on her shelf — warm, not hers. Emotional beat: quiet belonging; inheritance redefined as what you choose to carry forward.
